title: PostgreSQL vs DynamoDB vs Cassandra
description: Pick an engine from access pattern and the consistency/durability you can actually name. This is not a popularity ranking.

cells.workload: Relational rows, joins, unique constraints, multi-row transactions in one database. Ad-hoc query and reporting on the same model.
cells.consistency: Single-primary snapshot isolation (default READ COMMITTED). Replicas are lagged. Linearizable cluster-wide reads are not implied by 'the leader'.
cells.latency: Low ms for indexed primary-key lookups in-region. Joins and sequential scans dominate p99. Commit waits on WAL fsync and any synchronous replica.
cells.scaling: Vertical first. Read replicas for stale-tolerant reads. Write scale needs sharding or partitioning you operate.
cells.failure: Primary crash: promote a replica after fencing. Async replica promotion can lose acknowledged writes. Split-brain if two writers exist.
cells.costOps: You run backups, vacuum, failover, connection pooling, and major upgrades. Predictable instance + storage cost.
cells.whenNot: When the access pattern is a single-key item store at global write scale, or you cannot staff WAL, vacuum, and fenced failover.

cells.workload: Partition-key + optional sort-key item access, designed from queries first. Sparse indexes. Not SQL joins.
cells.consistency: Eventually consistent reads by default. Strongly consistent reads are same-region quorum reads, not global linearizability. Global tables are last-writer-wins.
cells.latency: Single-digit ms typical for in-region item ops when the partition is healthy. Hot keys and GSI backfill create tails.
cells.scaling: Partitions split with storage/throughput. You still own the partition key. Transactions are bounded (transact items), not arbitrary SQL.
cells.failure: Hot partition throttling, regional impairment, conflicting multi-region writes. No user-operated WAL promote.
cells.costOps: On-demand or provisioned WCU/RCU plus storage and indexes. Ops shift to data modeling, TTL, and capacity alarms rather than vacuum.
cells.whenNot: When you need multi-row relational constraints, ad-hoc SQL, or a globally linearizable ledger. Do not treat default reads as linearizable.

cells.workload: Wide-row, time-series-ish, high ingest with query tables designed up front. Availability-oriented multi-master writes.
cells.consistency: Tunable quorum (ONE/QUORUM/ALL) per request. QUORUM is not linearizable. Repairs and hinted handoff reconcile later. LWW/tombstones matter.
cells.latency: Good p50 ingest. p99 suffers from compaction, GC, and inconsistent replica sets. LOCAL_QUORUM in-region vs cross-DC ALL.
cells.scaling: Hash/vnode partitioning. Add nodes for write fan-out. You operate compaction and repair continuously.
cells.failure: Node loss is normal. Unavailable if you chose ALL. Counter and LWT paths have different failure stories. Delete tombstones can resurrect data if grace is wrong.
cells.costOps: High operator load: compaction, repair, JVM, disk. Multi-DC multiplies it. Managed C* reduces but does not delete the model constraints.
cells.whenNot: When you need foreign keys, multi-row ACID in one statement, or a small team that cannot run repair. TokenX spendable balances are a poor default here.

assumptions: Single-region numbers unless a cell says multi-region.
PostgreSQL default: one writable primary, streaming replicas, WAL on local disk.
DynamoDB default: eventual reads, provisioned or on-demand in one region; global tables are a separate mode.
Cassandra default: RF=3, client consistency named per query, not 'the cluster is consistent'.
Latency figures are order-of-magnitude interview planning numbers, not SLOs from a named production fleet.
